name: Use a sewing machine
blurb: Once you can thread it, wind a bobbin and set tension, a sewing machine does in minutes what hand sewing does in an evening. The machine is not delicate; the setup is.
gear: A basic sewing machine and its manual
steps: Read the manual for your specific machine, then wind a bobbin and thread the machine from scratch five times until it is automatic.
Learn the tension relationship: a balanced stitch looks the same on both sides. Loops on top mean bobbin tension issues; loops underneath usually mean the top thread is mis-threaded.
Sew straight lines on scrap paper without thread to practise steering and speed control.
Sew a straight seam on fabric, backstitching at both ends to lock it.
Learn to pivot at corners with the needle down, and to sew a curve slowly.
Make something real and simple: a cushion cover, a tote bag, or a hem.
tips: Nine out of ten machine problems are a rethread away. Unthread completely, with the presser foot up, and start again.
Change the needle regularly — a blunt needle causes skipped stitches and fabric damage.
Never pull the fabric through. Let the feed dogs do it or you will bend the needle.
proof: You make a finished item with straight, evenly tensioned seams and neat corners.
